title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 34
paragraphs: For the Naxians had not at all expected that this expedition would come against them. But when they were informed of it, they at once brought inside the walls the property that was in the fields, provided themselves with food and drink as for a siege, and strengthened their wall. So these were making preparations as for war about to fall on them; and the others meanwhile, having brought their ships over from Chios to Naxos, found them well defended when they attacked, and besieged them for four months. When the money the Persians had brought with them had all been used up, and Aristagoras himself had spent much in addition, and the siege kept demanding ever more, they built walls for the Naxian exiles and went back to the mainland, having failed.
